_about: THE TEST ID INDEX — every test identifier we use, what it asserts, where it runs, and how to run it. Created 2026-08-08 (user) after MAINNETSMOKE-01 and TXS-1 were quoted in chat and could not be found anywhere: they were not tasks, and TXS-* existed only as prose inside QA-XFAIL1.json's `next` field. A test id must resolve to something you can open — that is what this file is for. Viewer: tests.html. Naming convention (PROTOCOL.md): a bare CAPITALISED reference is a kPad TASK; a test id is written T:<id> in prose and chat, and must come with its URL. Each suite records what_it_does (the actual steps), pass_means, fails_when, its dimension and its cost — added 2026-08-08 after the user pointed out that 'real value, real network, once a day' does not tell anyone what the test IS.

convention.task: BARE CAPS — a kPad task, e.g. TXSTATUS-CONSOLIDATE1. Look it up in kPad.
convention.test: T:<id> — a test case, e.g. T:HBARXFER-01. Defined in this file; results on the QA grid.
convention.assertion: T:<suite>.<n> — one assertion inside a suite, e.g. T:A5b.4. Never a task.
convention.reproduction: A FAILING TEST MUST SAY HOW TO REPRODUCE IT. No red is reported — here, in chat, or on the dashboard — without concrete steps someone can follow. If the only way to trigger it is inside a harness, it is a harness artefact and must not be reported as a product failure (WC-RESETWEDGE1, 2026-08-08).

suites.title: The whole thing, end to end
suites.asserts: Two players join a board, one offers HBAR, both lock, the deal strikes, kWallet signs, it settles on Hedera.
suites.notes: Needs a game created on the TARGET's own backend — a board can only play a game its backend knows about, so pointing BASE elsewhere is not sufficient on its own.
what_it_does: Create a fresh public testnet game (own-to-own offers don't work, so every run needs a clean game two real players can join).
Player A opens the board and connects a wallet over WalletConnect — kWallet, our headless test wallet, does the pairing.
Player B opens the SAME board in a separate browser context and joins by typing an account (no wallet — a real second player).
A offers 0.01 HBAR to B via the asset card.
Both players lock. The deal strikes and the signing phase opens.
A taps Sign. kWallet auto-approves. The signature is saved and submitted.
The harness watches A's screen for the verdict toast.
suites.pass_means: A '🟩 Transaction successful' verdict appears on the board and the transfer is real on Hedera testnet. This is the only test that exercises the whole chain — board UI, lock rule, strike, WalletConnect, signing, submission, settlement, verdict.
suites.fails_when: Any link in that chain breaks. Historically its most common failure is harness fragility, not product breakage (see QA-HARNESSREPAIR1).
suites.how_to_reproduce: Run the harness listed above. If it fails, the run log names the failing assertion; the steps under 'What it does' are the manual equivalent.

suites.title: The wallet killed the session and never told us
suites.asserts: You clear connections in HashPack while katomia is CLOSED. Signing must fail fast and honestly instead of hanging. Eight assertions, A5b.1-A5b.8.

assertions.asserts: GHOST successfully created (dApp believes, wallet does not)
sign against a ghost does not hang — must give up inside the tx's validity window, not at the 120s cap
assertions.history: FAILED at exactly 120.0s on lab1 AND production (2026-08-07); the frozen benchmark's only expected_fail. FIXED by TXSTATUS-CONSOLIDATE1 S4 (KWC snapshot 33993b7) — passes on lab1 and pat 2026-08-08. Fixture also corrected to a 40s validity window, matching the board's real one; the SDK default 120s made the <60s assertion unreachable regardless of bundle behaviour.

assertions.asserts: sign against a ghost fails loudly, never silently succeeds
user can re-pair out of the ghost state
sign after re-pair reaches the wallet on the NEW session

what_it_does: Pair with the wallet and establish a real session.
Snapshot the dApp's WalletConnect storage (IndexedDB).
Destroy the session WALLET-SIDE, then restore the snapshot — so the dApp still believes it is connected but the wallet has no record. This is a true 'ghost'.
Attempt to sign against that ghost.
Re-pair and sign again.
suites.pass_means: The ghost sign gives up quickly and loudly, inside the transaction's own validity window — never hangs, never silently 'succeeds'. Then the user can re-pair and sign normally.
suites.fails_when: It hangs (was 120s until TXSTATUS-CONSOLIDATE1 S4), or worse, resolves as if it worked.
suites.why_it_matters: This is the discriminating ghost test — it reproduces the exact scenario where a user clears connections in HashPack while katomia is closed. T:WC-A5-ONLINE passes even on broken bundles; this one does not.
suites.harness_note: lives on the box at /opt/kwallet/ (not web-served — it runs its own in-process wallet peer)
suites.how_to_reproduce: Run the harness listed above. If it fails, the run log names the failing assertion; the steps under 'What it does' are the manual equivalent.

suites.title: The wallet was cleared while katomia was open
suites.asserts: The wallet's delete reaches us, so we should detect it and re-pair cleanly.
suites.state: 8/8 — healthy. Was SILENT for 14 days until 2026-08-08 (an unbounded hang ate the whole run and it reported nothing); harness given step ceilings, and a redundant resetWalletLink removed from its main flow. An A5.0 assertion added the same day was WITHDRAWN hours later: it failed only on accumulated harness state, not on any user path — see WC-RESETWEDGE1 for the full correction.
what_it_does: Pair, and sign once to prove the baseline works.
The USER CLEARS THE CONNECTION IN THEIR WALLET APP while the page is still open (simulated by a real wallet-side disconnect).
Try to sign again WITHOUT reloading and WITHOUT tapping Connect.
Re-pair and sign again.
Separately and last: call resetWalletLink(), reload, and re-initialise (assertion A5.0).
suites.pass_means: Step 3 detects the dead session, refuses to sign against it, and either self-heals onto a live session or reports KWC-GONE — never a silent wrong-session sign, never a hang.
suites.fails_when: The killed session survives in the dApp's storage and gets handed to every later sign (the pre-R2b bug: 'wallet says signed' then a wiped board).
suites.why_it_matters: Note this one passes on pre-fix bundles too, so treat it as a health check rather than proof the ghost handling works.
suites.harness_note: lives on the box at /opt/kwallet/ (not web-served — it runs its own in-process wallet peer)

assertions.asserts: dApp no longer reports a connected account after the wallet-side clear
no sign sent to the dead session
dApp surfaces an actionable error rather than hanging or lying
sign after recovery reaches the wallet on the NEW session

suites.title: Transaction validity-duration decode matrix
suites.asserts: 12 cases: Long int64 decode, SignedTransaction wrapper, cross-shape misuse fallbacks, absent field, garbage, real production fixture bytes, expiry arithmetic.
suites.reports: stdout only — not on the grid
what_it_does: Feed 12 shapes of transaction bytes to the validity-duration decoders: Long int64, SignedTransaction wrapper, cross-shape misuse, absent field, garbage, real production fixture bytes, and the expiry arithmetic.

suites.fails_when: A decoder silently returns the wrong window — which is how a transaction's real deadline and the UI's idea of it drift apart.

suites.title: Everyone at the table sees the same game
suites.asserts: Three scripted protocol-level clients on a fresh playnet game (joins, add accounts, offers, public + targeted chat, lock toggles): shared state converges identically on every client; per-socket fields (myPlayerId, targeted chat visibility) correctly differ.
suites.schedule: cron, daily 04:10 UTC (statsync-cron.sh) + on demand at every STATSYNC1-affecting change
what_it_does: Create a fresh public playnet game via POST /katomia/create.
Connect clients A, B, C over plain WebSocket (no browser) with distinct playerTokens.
A and B add playnet accounts (alice, bob); C stays a joined-but-accountless watcher.
Cross-offers (apple, banana), one public chat, one TARGETED chat B→A, lock on/off, a reject.
After quiescing, compare each client's final game_state.
suites.pass_means: Shared state (accounts/players/tx) is byte-identical across all three clients; myPlayerId is distinct per socket; the targeted chat reached A and its sender but never C.
suites.fails_when: Any client misses a broadcast, states diverge, or targeted chat leaks — exactly the properties an incremental-update refactor (STATSYNC1) could silently break.
suites.how_to_reproduce: cd qa/harness && node statsync-baseline.cjs — assertion lines print pass/fail with detail.

suites.title: What the full-state broadcast costs on the wire
suites.asserts: Message counts, bytes per broadcast, action→broadcast latency for a scripted sequence, plus a 30-chat growth probe showing broadcast size compounding with chat history. Recorded per STATSYNC1 phase; correctness may never regress, bytes must fall by P6.
what_it_does: Same scripted run as T:STATSYNC-01, with every websocket frame measured (bytes, latency).
Then 30 chat messages in a row, recording how each broadcast grows (full chat history rides every broadcast today).
Optionally spectates a live demo game passively (SAMPLE_GAME) for real-traffic sizes.
suites.pass_means: Baseline 2026-08-14: ~1.7-1.9KB/broadcast on a tiny 2-account game, ~2ms latency, growth probe 2071B→6525B over 30 chats (~154B per chat row, compounding). Later phases are judged against this file's benchmarks.
suites.fails_when: A phase re-run shows correctness failures, or (from P3 on) delta-path bytes fail to undercut the full-state baseline.
suites.how_to_reproduce: cd qa/harness && SAMPLE_GAME=q-crowd node statsync-baseline.cjs --record — summary JSON printed and written to qa/data/benchmarks/.

suites.title: A delta client sees exactly what a full-state client sees
suites.asserts: A probe client opted into game_delta (wantDelta:true at join) reconstructs state purely by patch application + chatAppend; at every seq its reconstruction is byte-identical to a full-state control client, and deltas undercut full states on the wire.
suites.schedule: cron, daily 04:10 UTC (statsync-cron.sh) + on demand at every STATSYNC1-affecting change
what_it_does: Client D joins with wantDelta:true after three full-state clients; its first broadcast is full, all subsequent are game_delta {seq, baseSeq, patch, chatAppend}.
D applies each patch (kpatch mirror of backend kdiff.js) and appends chat rows by monotonic id, trimming at 150 like the server.
After every broadcast, D's reconstructed shared view is compared against control client C's full game_state at the same seq.
suites.pass_means: One full state then only deltas; reconstruction ≡ control at every overlapping seq; visible chat matches (welcome rows excluded — legitimately per-viewer); delta bytes < full bytes. First green 2026-08-14: 39 deltas, 40/40 seqs identical, 374B vs 3696B avg (~90% saving).
suites.fails_when: Any patch mis-describes a change (reconstruction diverges), chatAppend leaks or drops a row, or a delta is sent to a socket without the right base seq.
suites.how_to_reproduce: cd qa/harness && node statsync-baseline.cjs — 02.x assertion lines print pass/fail; a seq mismatch names the exact seq.

suites.title: A client that misses a delta catches up and converges
suites.asserts: A delta client with a simulated lost broadcast detects the seq gap on the next delta, sends game_refresh exactly once (suppressing duplicates while the reply is in flight), receives a targeted full state, and converges with a full-state control client.
suites.schedule: cron, daily 04:10 UTC (statsync-cron.sh) + on demand at every STATSYNC1-affecting change
what_it_does: The delta probe silently drops one incoming game_delta (simulated network loss).
The next delta's baseSeq mismatches its local seq → it sends {type:'game_refresh', gameId} — once, with an in-flight guard, ignoring further deltas meanwhile.
The backend replies with a targeted full game_state (refresh:true) to that socket only and resets its delta base markers.
One more action confirms deltas apply cleanly again and the reconstruction matches control.
suites.pass_means: Exactly one refresh round-trip; no other client receives the refresh reply; post-recovery reconstruction is byte-identical to control. First green 2026-08-14.
suites.fails_when: Gap goes undetected (silent divergence — the worst failure mode of the whole refactor), refresh floods (no in-flight guard), the reply leaks to other sockets, or the client fails to resume deltas after recovery.
suites.how_to_reproduce: cd qa/harness && node statsync-baseline.cjs — 03.x assertion lines; DEBUG=1 prints the probe's per-message seq trace.

suites.title: The real board on deltas renders the same game as on full states
suites.asserts: Two headless board pages on one fresh playnet game — one plain, one ?delta=1 — stay state-identical through actions; the delta page provably runs on patches, self-heals a forced seq corruption via game_refresh, and throws zero page errors.
suites.schedule: cron, daily 04:10 UTC (statsync-cron.sh) + before any delta-default promotion
what_it_does: Create a fresh playnet game; a protocol driver client joins and owns two accounts.
Open the board twice headless (Playwright): plain URL and ?delta=1, both with __katomiaTestHooks so __qaGetState exposes state read-only.
Driver performs chats, add-account, an offer, a lock; after each settle the pages' accounts/players/tx and visible chat must match.
Then window.__stateSeq is forcibly corrupted on the delta page; the next broadcast must trigger one game_refresh and full reconvergence.
suites.pass_means: All six assertions green — first green 2026-08-14 (caught a real bug on the way: onmessage declared `const data`, so delta normalisation threw 'Assignment to constant variable' on every delta; states still converged, which is why the zero-page-errors assertion exists).
suites.fails_when: The delta page diverges from the full page, never actually consumes deltas, fails to self-heal a gap, or any page error fires.
suites.how_to_reproduce: cd qa/harness && node statsync-frontend.cjs — assertion lines print pass/fail; page errors are dumped verbatim on failure.

suites.title: Never guess a FAILED verdict — confirm on chain
suites.asserts: With the tx-receipt socket severed between sign and receipt, the board still reaches a SUCCESS verdict sourced from chain confirmation; FAILED is never shown for a tx the mirror confirms.
suites.state: LIVE since 2026-08-17 — verified green: per-tx receipt socket severed post-sign (_boardTxSocket.close(), which also stops its reconnect — the incident's no-reconnect shape); board reached truthful success via source "mirror" (⛓), never a guessed FAILED.
suites.why_it_matters: BOARD-TXTRUTH1 (2026-08-07): three false FAILURE verdicts on successful txs led to a real mainnet double spend — the only realized money harm to date. The fix (79858f4, confirm-on-chain) has no regression protection.

suites.title: Refuse to sign an expired transaction
suites.asserts: Tapping Sign after the validity window closes is refused with an expiry message: no signer:sign:saved success, no wallet round-trip.
suites.state: LIVE since 2026-08-17 — verified green: 40s window expired unsigned, external sign page (same paired context as the incident) refused with "expired Ns ago — window has closed"; zero signTx requests reached kWallet (kept manual so a slipped request parks as pending = fail).
suites.why_it_matters: SIGN-DEADTX1 (2026-08-07): Sign clicked 39s after window close saved the sig and logged success; the network could never accept it.

suites.title: The quiet ticket — stub on the chip, split stack, hover peek, one ticket at a time
suites.asserts: A priced asset's OWN chip wears the perforated right edge and no standalone ticket object exists; the cue costs zero chip height (measured at 390x844, the viewport the counter-band regression appeared on); the CSS mask does not clip the pick pennant off a pickable priced chip; tapping the priced chip opens its asset card carrying the ticket section and the maker's tear-up. A2: a stack with more than one unit splits when part of it is priced — two SOLID chips, the stub on exactly one, neither drawn as a dashed ghost (a ticket reserves nothing, so nothing has left the store), and no height cost. A3: hovering a priced chip opens a peek popover stating both legs, placed clear of the chip and pointer-events:none so it cannot swallow a drag, and lights every chip on the felt that could fill the ticket; both clear on leave. NFT snag: a thumb-only chip's ticket gutter is PAINTED and wide enough for the notch — the v8 skin gives thumb-only chips background:none and padding:0, so the mask was notching transparent air and the cue was invisible on NFTs. Multi-ticket: an asset carrying two tickets shows a tab per ticket and draws only ONE ticket's actions; switching tab switches which ticket is shown; and Remove from table is withheld while any ticket exists, saying why.
suites.notes: Phase A1 of docs/tickets-build-plan-20260821.html. Requires ?tickets=1. Guards three things that fail SILENTLY: (1) the standalone .board-ticket chip is gone — its whole job moved onto the give-leg's chip; (2) chip height must not change, because bandFull = tallest chip + 12 and a taller chip pushes store chips off a small screen (the P5a regression); (3) the mask must keep mask-clip:no-clip and a tile that reaches 24px left, or it eats the ::before pick pennant — which is invisible to every DOM and computed-style check, and did happen on the first cut. Screenshot artifact at qa/harness/tickets-quiet-last.png. A2 asserts D12 (the priced slice is solid, not a dashed ghost) — dashed already means 'gone from the store', and drawing a still-spendable slice as reserved would make the phase-B drag-out guard read as a surprise. Second screenshot at qa/harness/tickets-quiet-split.png. A3 is desktop-only by design (BOARD-TIPTOUCH1: on touch a hover cue fires on long-press and fights the drag). Third screenshot at qa/harness/tickets-quiet-peek.png.
what_it_does: Create a fresh unlisted playnet circle at 390x844; alice joins flagged (?tickets=1) and adds a manual account.
Turn Pickable ON first, so the pennant is already on the chip that is about to be masked.

Tap apple → 🎟 Price it… → want=banana → Create ticket.
Assert the apple chip carries .board-ticketed, no .board-ticket object exists anywhere, and the carrot chip is untouched.
Re-measure both chip heights and assert neither moved.
Assert the chip is both pickable and masked, that mask-clip is no-clip, and that the mask tile reaches further left than the pennant.
Tap the priced chip and assert the asset card opens carrying the ticket section and the tear-up action.
Save a screenshot for eyeball confirmation of the stub + pennant together.
Bring in a second player, run the ticket to settlement so the taker holds a stack of two apples (playnet seeds only one of each, so the stack has to be earned).
Price ONE apple and assert the stack renders as two chips, exactly one wearing the stub, neither ghosted, neither taller.

Open a third, hover-capable 1200px viewer and hover the priced chip: assert the peek appears, states both legs, sits clear of the chip, is pointer-events:none, and lights exactly the chips matching the WANT leg.
Move the pointer away and assert both the peek and the highlight clear.
Add the thumb-only class cascade a real NFT gets and assert the ticket gutter is painted, wide enough, and still masked (playnet has no NFTs, so this is emulated — worth one eyeball on testnet).
Price the same asset a SECOND time and assert two tabs appear, exactly one set of ticket actions is drawn, switching tabs switches the ticket, and Remove from table is withheld with a reason.
suites.pass_means: The ticket reads as a property of the item rather than an object beside it, without costing layout or eating another chip cue.
suites.fails_when: A cue is added that grows the chip; the mask clipping rule is weakened and the pennant silently disappears; or the asset card loses its ticket section. Or an asset with two tickets duplicates its action buttons again.

suites.title: The take as a gesture — drag both ways, and the double-promise guard
suites.asserts: B1: someone else's priced chip is draggable into your own space and lands the take EVEN THOUGH their store is not pickable (the ticket is the permission), producing the same fill group the asset-card button produces, with no auto-lock. B2: dragging an asset a ticket wants reveals exactly one wanted slot — the maker's own priced chip, not a new node — and dropping on it takes the ticket; the slot exists only during the drag. B3: offering out an asset you have priced asks first, names the unsourced outcome, and the ticket stays open and VISIBLY unsourced on both boards rather than vanishing. The unsourced ticket must read as an ABSENCE — red dashed and dimmed, distinct from the neutral offered-away ghost — not as a solid chip you still own.
suites.notes: Phase B of docs/tickets-build-plan-20260821.html. Requires ?tickets=1. HTML5 drag-and-drop cannot be driven by synthetic mouse events, so the gestures are exercised through the same dataTransfer contract the real drag uses — the chip's own ondragstart builds the payload and the target's ondrop consumes it. That covers what phase B adds (payload shape, drop routing, verb); the browser's dnd plumbing is not under test. B3 is driven at boardExecuteDrop directly, because a pie-slice hit test aimed at a bounding-box centre resolves to whichever wedge contains that point — drag plumbing, not the guard. Screenshot at qa/harness/tickets-gesture-unsourced.png.
what_it_does: Fresh playnet circle, two flagged players, both with a manual account. Alice prices her apple for a banana and leaves her store NOT pickable.
Assert her priced chip is draggable for Bob anyway, and that an unpriced chip of hers is not.
B1: drag the priced chip into Bob's own zone; assert two fill-cued rows on both boards and no auto-lock.
Recall to reopen the ticket.
B2: assert no wanted slot at rest; start dragging Bob's banana and assert exactly one slot appears, on the maker's priced chip; drop on it and assert the take; assert the slot clears.
Recall again.

B3: offer the priced apple out to Bob. Assert the confirm was raised, that it named the unsourced outcome, that the apple really left the store, that the ticket is still open, and that it renders as a visible unsourced chip on BOTH boards.
Assert the unsourced chip is dashed and dimmed in RED, and that the ordinary offered-away ghost is still the neutral dashed one.
suites.pass_means: One verb, two directions, and the collision between offering and pricing the same asset is surfaced rather than discovered at signing.
suites.fails_when: The take drag starts depending on allowPick again; wanted slots leak outside a drag; or an unsourced ticket becomes invisible because its give-leg has no store chip to hang on.
suites.how_to_reproduce: Run the harness. Each numbered assertion (T:TICKETS-GESTURE-01.n) prints PASS/FAIL with detail.

suites.title: Taking your own ticket with another account — allowed, and recorded as facts
suites.asserts: One player holding two accounts can take a ticket made on the other: the card offers BOTH tear-up and take, the take names the account, the maker's own account is never offered as the filler, and the fill settles like any other. The fill row carries provenance — sameInstigator plus each side's bound state at fill time — and nothing anywhere labels it a self-fill or a wash trade.
suites.notes: Phase C of docs/tickets-build-plan-20260821.html. Requires ?tickets=1, and a BACKEND change (katomiaActions.js writes prov on fill rows, katomia.js projects it) — run against a backend carrying both. The framing matters as much as the mechanics: two accounts under one player does NOT mean one entity owns both, because a player may be representing an account, so 'same player on both sides' is not evidence of self-dealing and the product must not assert that it is. Assertion 12 is the guard on that: the provenance object may contain no key that renders a verdict.
what_it_does: Fresh playnet circle; ONE flagged player adds TWO manual accounts (the footer control is a button with no accounts and a select once you hold one — the harness handles both).
Price the apple on the first account for a banana.
Open the priced chip's card and assert it offers tear-up AND take, that the take names the other account, and that the maker's own account is not a filler option.
Take it and assert a real two-row fill group.
Read the fill row's prov and assert it records sameInstigator and each side's bound state — and that it contains no self/wash/suspicion verdict.
Lock both accounts and assert the apple actually moved between them.
suites.pass_means: A player can try a ticket out end to end on their own, and the facts needed to judge such a fill later are captured at the moment it happens.
suites.fails_when: The take branch closes again because isMyAccount is per player; the maker's own account leaks into the filler list (a silent no-op fill); provenance stops being written or projected; or something starts calling it a self-fill.
suites.how_to_reproduce: Run the harness. Each numbered assertion (T:TICKETS-MULTIACCT-01.n) prints PASS/FAIL with detail.

suites.title: The settlement dial — Negotiable · Firm · Instant, and both interlocks
suites.asserts: Normal mode never sees the dial; nerd mode shows three positions with Firm selected. Negotiable leaves nobody locked. Firm locks the MAKER's side only and one taker action then settles it. Instant settles with no locking step at all. On a table where someone else is already locked, an Instant take STANDS DOWN — it neither settles nor leaves anyone auto-locked. Under lock rule 'all' the Instant position is disabled and says why, while Firm stays. Off playnet every position but Negotiable is refused, with a reason naming the signed-payload gap.
suites.notes: Phase D of docs/tickets-build-plan-20260821.html. Requires ?tickets=1 and a BACKEND carrying the orderFill wrapper in katomia.js. The dial is the whole proposal-to-order sliding scale on one maker-set control, and its real UI is the TAKE BUTTON'S LABEL — the maker decides, the taker consents by taking, so the button must state what taking does; the labels are asserted here. Two interlocks are safety, not polish: off playnet the dial is unsigned execution semantics (it is outside the signed payload AND an auto-lock carries no signed board basis, because it bypasses toggleLock), and Instant cannot be instant unless a connected pair may settle alone. Both are refused in the UI and again in the backend. The stand-down rule exists because resetLocksIfNeeded clears EVERY lock in the circle on any fill — auto-locking on a table someone else was mid-agreement on would be consenting to a board nobody has seen. PROP-LOCKSCOPE1 is the properly engineered fix, after which this can relax to 'this cluster is quiet'.
what_it_does: Assert the dial is absent in normal mode and present with three positions and Firm preselected in nerd mode.
Negotiable: create, take, assert nobody locked and the button said 'haggle'.
Firm (fresh circle): assert the button says 'at this price', the maker's side locks, the taker's does not, nothing settled yet, and ONE taker lock then settles it.
Instant (fresh circle): assert the button says it settles instantly, and that it settles with no locking step.
Stand-down (fresh circle): lock someone else first, then take an Instant ticket — assert it did NOT settle and left nobody auto-locked.
Lock rule 'all': assert Instant is disabled with a reason and Firm still offered.
Drive the availability rule with a stubbed mainnet gameMeta and assert only Negotiable survives, with a reason naming the signing gap.
suites.pass_means: The maker can choose how far along the proposal-to-order scale a ticket sits, the taker is never surprised by it, and the lever cannot produce unsigned execution semantics or an unkeepable promise.
suites.fails_when: A dial position stops matching its button label; the stand-down rule regresses and a take auto-locks over someone else's torn-up lock; or either interlock is weakened so a non-Negotiable ticket can be posted off playnet or under a lock rule that cannot honour it.
suites.how_to_reproduce: Run the harness. Each numbered assertion (T:TICKETS-DIAL-01.n) prints PASS/FAIL with detail.
